denomProfiles/presbyterian-church-of-kor: Fervent prayer, self-supporting growth and missionary zeal in Korea's largest Protestant family.
The Westminster Confession and Catechisms, with the 1907 Twelve Articles of the first Korean presbytery.
Authority and (in Hapdong especially) inerrancy of Scripture.
Calvinist teaching on grace, election and covenant.
Infant baptism and the Lord's Supper as the two sacraments.
Strict Sabbath observance and tithing as marks of discipleship.
Evangelism and church growth, producing some of the world's largest congregations.
Overseas mission: Korea is among the largest senders of Protestant missionaries.
Prayer as the engine of church life.
Education through seminaries such as Presbyterian University and Theological Seminary (Tonghap) and Chongshin (Hapdong).
Daily dawn prayer meetings (saebyeok gido), a practice associated with Gil Seon-ju.
Tongsong kido: the whole congregation praying aloud together.
Cell groups (guyeok) led by lay leaders and pastoral home visitation.
Wednesday and Friday overnight services and prayer retreats on mountains.
Tonghap ordains women ministers (from the 1990s); Hapdong does not.
Korean diaspora churches
Korean Presbyterian congregations spread across the Americas, Japan and Central Asia.
Presbyterian Church in the Republic of Korea
The more liberal Kijang split away in 1953 and became a home of minjung theology.
Global mission movement
Korean missionaries planted Presbyterian churches across Asia, Africa and Latin America.
Horace G. Underwood
Pioneer American Presbyterian missionary (arrived 1885).
Samuel A. Moffett
Missionary founder of the Pyongyang seminary.
Gil Seon-ju
Leader of the 1907 revival and one of the first seven Korean ministers.
Joo Ki-chul
Pastor who refused Shinto shrine worship and died in prison in 1944.
Han Kyung-chik
Founder of Youngnak Presbyterian Church and 1992 Templeton Prize laureate.
denomProfiles/french-reformed/tagline: The Huguenot church: persecution, exile, resistance and a memory of the 'Desert'.
denomProfiles/french-reformed/coreDoctri: The Gallican Confession (Paris 1559, ratified at La Rochelle 1571).
Scripture alone as the rule of faith, read with the early creeds.
Salvation by grace through faith, in Calvin's tradition.
Two sacraments, with Christ spiritually present in the Supper.
Freedom of conscience, a conviction sharpened by centuries of persecution.
denomProfiles/french-reformed/focuses/0: Religious liberty and laïcité, which French Protestants long supported.
denomProfiles/french-reformed/focuses/1: Memory of persecution and resistance (Musée du Désert, Tour de Constance).
denomProfiles/french-reformed/focuses/2: Rescue and hospitality, notably Le Chambon-sur-Lignon's sheltering of Jews in the Second World War.
denomProfiles/french-reformed/focuses/3: Union with Lutherans in the United Protestant Church of France (2013).
denomProfiles/french-reformed/practices/: Sober worship in temples, with sermon, psalms and the Genevan melodies.
Presbyterian-synodal government by local councils and regional and national synods.
Celebration of the Lord's Supper typically monthly or at feasts.
Ordination of women pastors; since 2015 congregations may bless same-sex couples.
denomProfiles/french-reformed/influenced: Exiles after 1685 strengthened Protestant communities in the Netherlands, Prussia, England, the Cape and the Carolinas.
Camisard prophets who fled to London influenced the circle from which the Shakers emerged.
Its national synod system influenced Reformed polity elsewhere.
denomProfiles/french-reformed/keyFigures: French reformer whose Geneva shaped Huguenot doctrine.
Calvin's successor, presiding at the Synod of La Rochelle (1571).
Admiral and Huguenot leader killed in the St Bartholomew's Day Massacre (1572).
Restorer of the clandestine 'Church of the Desert' after 1715.
Pastor of Le Chambon-sur-Lignon during the rescue of Jews.
denomProfiles/swiss-reformed/tagline: Cradle of Reformed Protestantism: Zwingli's Zurich, Calvin's Geneva, cantonal churches today.
denomProfiles/swiss-reformed/coreDoctrin: Scripture as the sole norm, proclaimed in Zwingli's Zurich disputations (1523).
The Second Helvetic Confession (1566) as a historic standard, though most cantonal churches no longer bind clergy to confessions.
A spiritual understanding of Christ's presence in the Supper (Consensus Tigurinus, 1549).
Rejection of images in worship and of the Mass as sacrifice.
God's sovereignty and covenant grace, in the tradition of Zwingli and Bullinger.
denomProfiles/swiss-reformed/focuses/0: Public and cantonal responsibility: churches are recognised under cantonal law.
denomProfiles/swiss-reformed/focuses/2: Academic theology at Zurich, Basel, Bern and Geneva.
denomProfiles/swiss-reformed/focuses/3: Ecumenical engagement; Geneva hosts the World Council of Churches.
denomProfiles/swiss-reformed/practices/0: Plain churches cleared of images, with the pulpit at the centre.
denomProfiles/swiss-reformed/practices/1: The Lord's Supper, historically celebrated a few times a year, now more frequent in many parishes.
denomProfiles/swiss-reformed/practices/2: Congregational singing of psalms and hymns.
denomProfiles/swiss-reformed/practices/3: Self-governing cantonal churches federated since 2020 as the Protestant Church in Switzerland (EKS).
denomProfiles/swiss-reformed/practices/4: Women ordained since 1918 in Zurich and now in all cantonal churches.
denomProfiles/swiss-reformed/influenced/: Zwingli's radical followers broke away in Zurich in 1525.
John Knox brought Genevan models to Scotland in 1560.
It adopted the Second Helvetic Confession in 1567.
Karl Barth and Emil Brunner reshaped twentieth-century Protestant theology.
denomProfiles/swiss-reformed/keyFigures/: Zwingli's successor and author of the Second Helvetic Confession.
Basel theologian and principal author of the Barmen Declaration.
Zurich theologian of the dialectical school.
denomProfiles/swiss-reformed/inIndia: The Basel Mission, a Swiss-German Reformed and Lutheran society, worked in coastal Karnataka and northern Kerala from 1834; its congregations now belong largely to the Church of South India.
denomProfiles/anglican/tagline: A worldwide family of churches, catholic and reformed, joined by common prayer.
denomProfiles/anglican/coreDoctrines/0: Scripture 'containeth all things necessary to salvation' (Article VI), read with the creeds and the Fathers.
denomProfiles/anglican/coreDoctrines/1: The Chicago–Lambeth Quadrilateral (1888): Scripture, the creeds, the two dominical sacraments and the historic episcopate.
denomProfiles/anglican/coreDoctrines/2: Justification by faith (Article XI), held across evangelical and catholic emphases.
denomProfiles/anglican/coreDoctrines/3: Doctrine expressed through worship: lex orandi, lex credendi.
denomProfiles/anglican/coreDoctrines/4: Autonomous national provinces bound by 'bonds of affection' rather than a central jurisdiction.
denomProfiles/anglican/focuses/0: Holding together evangelical, Anglo-Catholic and liberal traditions.
denomProfiles/anglican/focuses/1: Mission and education, historically through CMS, SPG/USPG and other societies.
denomProfiles/anglican/focuses/2: Ecumenism, from the Lambeth Quadrilateral to dialogues with Rome and the Orthodox.
denomProfiles/anglican/focuses/3: Continuing debates over women's ordination and human sexuality.
denomProfiles/anglican/practices/0: Liturgical worship descended from the Book of Common Prayer.
denomProfiles/anglican/practices/1: Episcopal ordination of bishops, priests and deacons.
denomProfiles/anglican/practices/2: Lambeth Conference of bishops, roughly every ten years since 1867.
denomProfiles/anglican/practices/3: Infant baptism and confirmation by a bishop.
denomProfiles/anglican/practices/4: Choral, sung office and Eucharist in many places.
denomProfiles/anglican/influenced/0/text: Methodism began as a renewal movement within the Church of England.
denomProfiles/anglican/influenced/1/text: Anglican dioceses joined the first union of episcopal and non-episcopal churches (1947).
denomProfiles/anglican/influenced/2/text: Several West African prophetic churches arose among Anglicans.
denomProfiles/anglican/influenced/3/text: The Lambeth Quadrilateral became a widely cited basis for church union.
denomProfiles/anglican/keyFigures/0/role: Author of the Book of Common Prayer.
denomProfiles/anglican/keyFigures/1/role: Theologian of Of the Laws of Ecclesiastical Polity (1594–).
denomProfiles/anglican/keyFigures/2/role: Archbishop of Canterbury who called the first Lambeth Conference (1867).
denomProfiles/anglican/keyFigures/4/role: Archbishop of Cape Town and anti-apartheid leader.
denomProfiles/anglican/members/note: The Anglican Communion Office's commonly cited figure of about 85 million members in some 42 provinces; it counts many nominal baptised members in England.
denomProfiles/anglican/inIndia: Anglicanism came with East India Company chaplains and the missions of the CMS and SPG; the Diocese of Calcutta was founded in 1814. Its Indian dioceses entered the Church of South India (1947) and the Church of North India (1970), both members of the Communion.
denomProfiles/church-of-england/tagline: England's established church: parish, Prayer Book and the mother of Anglicanism.
denomProfiles/church-of-england/coreDoct: The Thirty-nine Articles (1571), the Book of Common Prayer (1662) and the Ordinal as historic formularies.
Scripture as containing all things necessary to salvation, read with the catholic creeds.
Two sacraments of the Gospel, baptism and the Lord's Supper, with five other rites.
The threefold ministry of bishops, priests and deacons in apostolic succession.
The monarch as Supreme Governor, under parliamentary establishment.
denomProfiles/church-of-england/focuses/: A parish ministry to every community in England.
Church schools: about a quarter of England's primary schools.
Public role: 26 bishops sit in the House of Lords.
Debates on sexuality, including the Prayers of Love and Faith for same-sex couples (2023).
denomProfiles/church-of-england/practice: Morning and Evening Prayer and Holy Communion, using the BCP or Common Worship (2000).
Choral Evensong in cathedrals and collegiate chapels.
Infant baptism, confirmation by a bishop, weddings and funerals for parishioners.
Government by bishops and the General Synod (since 1970).
Women priests since 1994 and bishops since 2015.
denomProfiles/church-of-england/influenc: John and Charles Wesley were Church of England priests.
Puritan Separatists left the established church from the 1580s.
Colonial Anglicanism became the American Episcopal Church.
J. N. Darby left the Church of Ireland ministry to found the Brethren movement.
Its missions and colonial churches became the worldwide Communion.
denomProfiles/church-of-england/keyFigur: Archbishop of Canterbury and architect of the Prayer Book.
Queen whose 1559 settlement fixed the church's character.
Tractarian leader who became a Roman Catholic in 1845.
Archbishop of Canterbury and author of Christianity and Social Order (1942).
denomProfiles/church-of-england/members/: Average weekly attendance of about one million (all ages) in the Church of England's Statistics for Mission 2023; many more identify as Anglican in surveys.
denomProfiles/church-of-england/inIndia: Company chaplains built St Mary's, Fort St George, Madras (1680), and CMS and SPG missions worked in Tamil Nadu and Kerala; the Church of India, Burma and Ceylon (autonomous from 1930) later joined the CSI and CNI.
denomProfiles/scottish-episcopal/tagline: Small, disestablished Anglican church in Scotland that gave America its first bishop.
denomProfiles/scottish-episcopal/coreDoc: Anglican faith expressed in the Scottish liturgies rather than in a binding confession.
The historic episcopate, preserved by the nonjuring bishops after 1689.
A high view of the Eucharist, with an epiclesis (invocation of the Spirit) in the Scottish Communion Office.
Scripture, creeds and tradition read with reason.
Since 2017 its canon law allows clergy to marry same-sex couples.
denomProfiles/scottish-episcopal/focuses: Ministry across Scotland's seven dioceses, often in rural areas.
Ecumenical relations with the Church of Scotland and others.
An inclusive stance on women's ministry and sexuality.
denomProfiles/scottish-episcopal/practic: Scottish Liturgy 1982 and the Scottish Prayer Book (1929).
Bishops elected by diocesan synods; one bishop serves as Primus.
Women priests since 1994 and bishops since 2018.
Weekly sung Eucharist in most congregations.
denomProfiles/scottish-episcopal/influen: Its bishops consecrated Samuel Seabury in Aberdeen (1784), and its eucharistic prayer shaped the 1789 American Prayer Book.
The Scottish rite was a model for later liturgical revision.
denomProfiles/scottish-episcopal/keyFigu: Bishop and liturgical scholar behind the Scottish rite.
Primus who led the consecration of Samuel Seabury (1784).
Primus during the repeal of the penal laws (1792).
First American bishop, consecrated in Aberdeen.
denomProfiles/scottish-episcopal/inIndia: The church supported a mission at Chanda (now Chandrapur, Maharashtra) from the 1870s, whose congregations passed into the Church of North India.
